THE HARD CALL, DO NOT DUCK IT: ioc-extraction-reliability now has genuinely 2 independent sources (src-0003 LANCE/PRISM 97.6% F1, and src-0007 vanilla-LLM IoC extraction precision 0.8240 GPT-4o / 0.8503 o3-mini / 0.8846 GPT-4o-FT / 0.6944 GPT-4o-mini-FT over 1310 expert-annotated IoCs), which is the rubric's stated bar for 3, up from the single-source 2 it has held since cycle 4. But ctr-0001 is open against it and config.yml gates.g3_contradiction_demotion is 2, which on the T4 prompt's wording ('loses g3_contradiction_demotion points') mechanically yields 1. READ THIS BEFORE YOU DO THE ARITHMETIC: the prompt and the validator do not agree on what the g3 gate means, and cycle 9 checked the code rather than assuming. prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 describes a SUBTRACTION (3 - 2 = 1). scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 implement a CEILING instead: it only errors if an issue with an open contradiction scores above scale_max - demotion, i.e. above 3. So the validator would accept 1, 2 or 3 here and reject only 4 or 5, and the current score of 2 is already compliant. Do not assume the validator forces 1. Follow the T4 prompt's subtraction as the governing rule if you find it persuasive, but say in the rationale which of the two readings you applied and that you knew they differ -- and if you conclude the prompt and validator genuinely disagree in a way that matters, note it as a carry-forward for a cycle with standing to reconcile them rather than editing either file yourself. Both readings are defensible and you must pick one EXPLICITLY IN THE RATIONALE and say why, rather than silently landing on a number. Arguments you must actually engage, not just recite: FOR the demotion -- the two sources disagree in magnitude about the same underlying quantity (a bare LLM at 0.82-0.88 precision lands at or below the 86% VirusTotal baseline that src-0003 presents as the tool it beats), and until someone does the head-to-head the issue's headline claim is less settled than a naive 2-source count suggests; the whole point of a demotion gate is that unresolved conflict is worse than clean single-source evidence. AGAINST a full demotion -- ctr-0001's own text names three confounds (SYSTEM: LANCE is regex+LLM+human-validation while src-0007's Table 4 is explicitly headed 'Vanilla LLMs'; METRIC: 97.6% is F1 while 0.82-0.88 is precision with no recall or F1 reported anywhere for that task; CORPUS: 50 public threat reports vs an unnamed company's internal workflow) and states that if the SYSTEM confound is confirmed as the explanation the contradiction should be CLOSED and folded into the issue's third candidate_resolution rather than left open. Prompt line 22 says when torn, give the lower one. Whatever you decide, state the pre-demotion score and the post-demotion score separately in the rationale so the arithmetic is auditable, and note that this is the first time the g3 gate has ever fired in this project. ALSO RE-SCORE THESE, they are affected even though cycle 9 did not edit them: (a) ttp-attack-mapping-reliability, currently 3 on src-0002+src-0005 -- src-0007 is unclaimed third-source evidence for it, reporting MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification precision 0.2787 / recall 0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480 / 0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387 / 0.1846 (GPT-4o FT), 0.1771 / 0.1414 (GPT-4o-mini FT) on real production CTI material, far below CTIBench's 0.6388 F1 ceiling. This is NOT a contradiction (different benchmarks over different corpora, and real-world material being harder than a curated benchmark is the expected direction) but it is a third independent source measuring the same sub-task, and T4 may cite it in the rationale even though the graph's candidate_resolutions do not yet list it -- flag in your rationale that a T2/T3 should attach it properly. (b) task-dependent-reliability-framing, currently 3 -- src-0007 is a fourth WITHIN-STUDY demonstration of task-dependence (same team, same corpus, same four models, same Table 4: IoC extraction 0.82-0.88 precision vs TTP identification 0.2787/0.2270), and critically it cuts IN FAVOUR of the 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation' ordinal axis that cycle 7 and cycle 8 recorded as being in doubt on the strength of src-0006. Do not simply inherit the prior rationale's one-sided reading; weigh src-0007 against src-0006's cross-stage finding and say in the rationale that the two are not obviously reconcilable. Be stingy per prompt line 21-22 -- this is a reason the issue is more interesting, not automatically a reason it scores higher, and the split recommendation below still applies. CARRY-FORWARD ITEMS, PRESERVE ALL OF THESE IN YOUR OWN LOG so they survive to a cycle with standing to act on them (T4 has no standing to restructure the graph; only a T2 does): [1] SPLIT task-dependent-reliability-framing into two issues -- its single score averages the NARROW claim (CTI reliability varies by sub-task; independently supported by src-0001, src-0002, src-0006 and now src-0007; merits 3) against the SPECIFIC ordinal axis (mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation), which src-0006's Table 5 disputes by marking failure subtypes as spanning all four pipeline stages (e.g. 'Co-mention bias (Type 1.1) -- stages 1234') while src-0007's Table 4 supports it; on its own the axis would score 1.
